d.d: To attempt; to endeavour. Followed by infinitive.
d.x: I tried to rollerblade, but I couldn’t.

d.d: To make an experiment. Usually followed by a present participle.
d.x: I tried mixing more white paint to get a lighter shade.
I shall try my skills on this.
I gave unicycling a try but I couldn’t do it.

d.d: An act of tasting or sampling.
d.x: I gave sushi a try but I didn’t like it.

d.d: A score in rugby league and rugby union, analogous to a touchdown in American football.
d.x: Today I scored my first try.

d.d: present participle and gerund of try
The act by which one tries something; an attempt.
A test of the suitability or effectiveness of a person or thing, especially an audition for a performer or athlete, or the advance staging of a play at a small theatre.
A digestive enzyme that cleaves peptide bonds (a serine protease)

An essential amino acid with an indole side chain; present in many foods, especially chocolate, oats, banana and milk; it is essential for normal growth and development and is the precursor of serotonin and niacin; any specific form of this compound, or any derivative of it.
A prearranged meeting or assignation, now especially between lovers to meet at a specific place and time.
A market fair, especially a recurring one held on a schedule, where livestock sales took place.
To make a tryst; to agree to meet at a place.
To arrange or appoint (a meeting time etc.).
To keep a tryst, to meet at an agreed place and time.
